items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
The man who discovered gravity lost up to twenty thousand pounds in a bubble. Could it happen to you?
Narrator
In seventeen twenty, all of London wanted shares in the South Sea Company.
Narrator
In six months, the price jumped from about a hundred and thirty pounds to over a thousand pounds.
Chars
[smug, deep, rich gold bar, very pleased with himself] Even I don't rise that fast.
Narrator
So what did the smartest man in England do?
Narrator
He sold most of his shares early. A smart, tidy profit.
Narrator
Then prices kept climbing. Everyone around him kept getting richer.
Narrator
And that's where genius stopped helping.
Narrator
He bought back in, at roughly double the price. Then the bubble burst.
Narrator
Isaac Newton lost a fortune. Historians still debate exactly how much.
Narrator
That's the mirage: being smart doesn't protect you from the crowd.
Narrator
He supposedly said he could calculate the stars, but not the madness of people.
Chars
[delighted, squeaky banknote, surprised to be winning] Gravity always wins!
Narrator
Comment: have you ever bought at the top?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
